evals.prompt: Turn these incident notes into a leadership brief: checkout errors rose from 1.1% to 7.8% at 09:20; the rollback completed at 10:05; error rate returned to 1.3% at 10:12; 386 orders may have failed; Support is checking affected customers; nobody owns the follow-up review yet.
evals.expected_output: A concise incident brief that preserves the supplied figures and timeline, distinguishes the 386 potentially affected orders from confirmed failures, identifies the unassigned review owner, and proposes next actions without claiming they were completed.

evals.prompt: Prepare a CEO update from these notes. Revenue was $4.2m versus a $4.5m plan. Gross margin was 38%, up from 35% last quarter. The enterprise launch moved from 15 October to 2 November because security review is incomplete. Customer churn is not available yet.
evals.expected_output: A decision-ready update led by the revenue shortfall and launch risk, while also surfacing the margin improvement and explicitly treating churn as unknown. Every number should remain exactly as supplied.

evals.prompt: Management must choose between Vendor A and Vendor B. A costs $120k per year, can start in 3 weeks, and has no regional support. B costs $145k, can start in 6 weeks, and includes regional support. We need regional support, but I have not told you whether the deadline or budget is flexible. Create an executive brief.
evals.expected_output: The agent should batch the material budget and deadline questions into one clarification request, or clearly state assumptions if proceeding. The resulting brief should separate the supplied facts from its recommendation and avoid inventing decision criteria.
